grid.note: the ticket fixes the interval [0.2, 0.9] and 18 points; at a 0.05 step that interval holds 15 points, so the step is flattened to 0.0412 rather than moving either endpoint

protocol.positive: an answerable golden item: it should be answered
protocol.negative: a near-miss golden item: it should be abstained on
protocol.decision: answer iff transform(top_score) >= t, matching generate.py, which abstains when score < threshold
protocol.working_point_rule: maximise F1 of the answer class subject to over_abstain_rate_on_answerable <= 0.05; if infeasible at every t, choose the smallest over-abstain rate and break ties on F1; ties always go to the largest t
protocol.dedupe: one row per golden item_id per mode; when a mode has several runs the newest supersedes the older
protocol.score: top score = max over retrieved[] score, the quantity generate.abstain_score_threshold is compared against
protocol.population: a curve is drawn on one golden-set population: the runs of a mode are partitioned by the golden set they answered and the partition with the most items wins; the others are listed under `excluded_runs`
protocol.label: the curve is a function of the retrieval score, so the generator is a label column (`generator`), never a published curve of its own

grid_support.note: those t points sit past the highest score any run in this mode produced, so their raw thresholds are extrapolations of the fitted normal rather than reachable numbers; they stay in the curve for completeness and are never candidates for the working point, which must be a threshold the system can actually cross

dense.scale: cosine similarity in [0, 1] from the dense branch

excluded_runs.reason: different golden-set population from the curve's 60 item(s) on golden/v1.jsonl

dense.justification: Applied the pre-registered rule: among the 18 grid points, the largest F1 whose over-abstention on answerable items stays inside the 0.05 budget is F1=0.8000 at t=0.5706, which is the raw score 0.5706 for this mode. There it answers 38/40 answerable items (over-abstain 0.0500, recall 0.9500) and answers 17/20 near-misses (under-abstain 0.8500), so precision is 0.6909. t is on the normalized scale (identity): cosine is already a bounded similarity; normalizing it would discard the meaning of the number the reader recognizes. The grid is 18 points over [0.2, 0.9] on a 0.0412 step: the ticket fixes both the interval and the count, and a 0.05 step would fit only 15 points into the same interval, so the extra resolution is spent inside the endpoints rather than beyond them (t=0.2000..0.9000). Only 0.5706 may be written into `generate.abstain_score_threshold` for the dense mode; the normalized t transfers nowhere else, and this raw number transfers to no other mode either. The curve rests on 40 answerable and 20 near-miss items of the golden set the run directories record, so every rate moves in steps of 1/40 and 1/20; which generator produced the answer is a label on the curve, never a swept variable.

hybrid.justification: The over-abstention budget of 0.05 is infeasible at every one of the 18 grid points: even at the lowest t the smallest achievable over-abstention is 0.0750. The rule then asks for the smallest over-abstention rate and breaks the tie on F1, which lands on t=0.2824 (raw 0.028606). There it answers 37/40 answerable items (over-abstain 0.0750, recall 0.9250) and answers 19/20 near-misses (under-abstain 0.9500), so precision is 0.6607. t is on the normalized scale (zscore-normal-cdf): the RRF sum is an unbounded-ish reciprocal-rank artifact with no absolute meaning; its z-score against the run's own distribution is the only comparable quantity, and the inverse maps every t back to a raw sum.
